discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies with WMAP, establishing the standard LambdaCDM cosmological model
motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe transformed cosmology into a precision science. Under Bennett's leadership, with Page's instrument design and calibration and Spergel's analysis framework, WMAP measured the temperature and polarization anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background over the full sky with unprecedented control of systematics. Its results fixed the age, geometry and composition of the universe to percent precision: a spatially flat cosmos dominated by dark energy and cold dark matter, with nearly scale-invariant adiabatic Gaussian primordial fluctuations, and the epoch of reionization. Independently of supernovae, WMAP confirmed that most of the universe consists of unknown dark energy and dark matter, and supplied the calibrated framework in which all subsequent cosmological measurements, including Planck, baryon acoustic oscillations and supernova surveys, are interpreted. It is a model of how a new, carefully engineered observational capability, followed through with statistical rigour, changes our understanding of fundamental physics.
